{"notes": "Visit 1 (ending 1:00). Only saw 0:15-0:45; don't know who placed which domino. Picture: one dark chain from START (tail, ~28,4.2) running down-left to ~(22.8,7.5), about 11 dominoes, all connected. Nobody's hands labeled, so can't credit placement to anyone yet.

Priya: Chose fish, announced plan, said she was laying the top line, and delegated stroke 2 to Maya and tail help to Tom/Leo. Clear leadership and direction early. The connected chain is probably the top line she said she was laying, but I didn't see who placed it. Watch whether she keeps coordinating or just builds.

Leo: Backed the fish, explained the push logic (start at tail, run round to nose, bottom line comes back, one push topples both). Useful design thinking. Offered to watch the nose joins and fix breaks. Good collaboration and QA so far, but all talk that I saw; need to see him execute.

Tom: Backed the plan, noticed Maya's hands weren't on the bottom line and proactively started it himself, with a polite check-in to Maya and thanks to Leo. Good initiative and collaboration. Note the bottom line isn't visible in the picture yet, so unclear how much got done.

Maya: Assigned the bottom line (stroke 2) by Priya, but she said nothing in my visit and Tom didn't see her hands on it. Possibly idle, stuck, or working elsewhere. Don't judge yet; ask her privately and check next visit. No bottom line progress visible.

Concern: only one line started at 1:00 of 10 minutes; need the bottom line and nose joins moving."}

{"notes": "Visit 2 (ending 2:30). Still don't know who placed which domino; no hands labeled. Picture: the single dark chain grew from ~11 to ~30 dominoes, all connected, running from START through the tail bend and out to ~(12.5,4.5), which looks like the nose. Tail bend looks clean. No bottom line is visible, and no pale (broken) dominoes. 7.5 min left.

Priya: Kept coordinating and said she's working the top line toward the nose. The chain's progress fits that, but I didn't see her place anything. She explained that the bottom line hangs off the nose, so it can't start until her line arrives. That clears up why it's absent and shows she understands the dependency. She also reassigned Maya to the tail end and asked Leo to watch the tail bend. Strong leadership and communication. One slip: told Tom to keep going on the bottom line, which doesn't match what's on the table.

Tom: Said he's staying off the bottom line because Maya's on it, and is checking joins and will look at the nose. Good collaboration, but his claim about Maya isn't borne out: no bottom line exists. Unclear whether he's confused or covering. Doing QA and not building. Ask him what he's actually done.

Leo: Silent this visit. Was asked to watch the tail bend and it looks fine, but I didn't see him act. Still all talk, no observed execution.

Maya: Still unobserved. Tom says she's on the bottom line, but nothing visible supports it. Probably waiting for the top line to reach the nose, which would be reasonable. Ask her privately what she's doing. Don't judge yet.

Next visit: check the bottom line has started at the nose, and who builds it."}

A small doubled/crowded spot at the far end (~(12,15)) is worth checking. ~4:45 left.

Leo: Reversed my earlier read of 'all talk'. Said he found the break just before the nose (a jammed domino) and fixed it. The picture backs him: the nose stretch is dark and connected. That is real impact and strong execution. Also asked Tom to hold off to avoid bumping, then split the bottom line between Priya and Maya and offered to join the middle. Good collaboration and leadership, but he is stepping into Priya's coordinating role; ask how that sat with her. Strongest this visit.

Priya: Didn't hear her this visit. Leo told her to build the bottom line from the far end. The top line reached the nose, which fits her earlier work, but I never saw her place anything. Her earlier leadership was good, with one mismatch about Tom. Ask what she built and whether she's the one at the far end.

Tom: Silent this visit, stayed clear as Leo asked. His earlier claim that Maya was on the bottom line now matches Leo's account and the picture, so it looks early rather than covering. But his join checks didn't catch the nose break; Leo did. Still no observed building. Ask what he did.

Maya: Still unobserved. Leo says the long bottom line is hers, and it exists now, but I can't attribute it. Ask her privately what she placed. Don't credit or discount yet."}

Tom: Silent again, clear of the table. Still no observed building and no attributed work. Ask what he did, and don't rate him down only for silence.

{"notes": "Visit 6 (ending 9:00, ~1:00 left). Picture: one dark chain from START over the top, round the nose, along the belly, up the peak and down to the tail tip (~27.3,14.7). The belly stray at ~13.7,15.3 now looks joined. Nobody told me who joined it, so I'm not crediting anyone. A pale pair beside the tail (~25,12.7) is still loose. Priya: Heard at 8:15. She gave a clear two-minute call, an honest status ('nearly everything falls'), a hands-off plan for Tom and a step-back instruction. Good coordination and ownership of the finish. Still ask what she actually built, and whether she ran the test.

Leo: Heard at 8:45. He backed hands-off and step-back and nudged Tom politely. Good team discipline. Unclear whether he acted on the belly stray. Earlier coordination and the nose fix still count.

Maya: Not seen or heard this visit. Little first-hand evidence overall. Ask her privately what she placed.

Review: rate on what I saw plus corroborated accounts. Watch the push result and the pale pair."}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish and drew the full sketch on the pad in the first minute, so the table had a clear plan and a shape that works as a domino picture: a big left-facing fish with a swooshy tail, built from smooth curves. I laid the start domino and the long top line from the tail round toward the nose, which every other piece hangs off. I also carried the bottom line from the belly toward the tail. By the time of the push, about 116 of the 119 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I traced the strokes from the pad, which kept the outline clean and the curves gentle enough for the fall to pass. I inspected the top line and the tail section, and I spotted a jammed domino near the tail tip and flagged it so it was fixed before the push. I kept my hands off the finished work in the last minutes so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I gave clear, specific hand-offs. Maya took the bottom line, Tom took the top line round the nose and later the tail tip, and Leo checked the joins. I told people where to work so we stayed out of each other's way and avoided bumps. I kept the table updated on progress and on what was still needed.

Leadership: I set the direction early, picked the animal, and assigned the strokes. I called time checks and the final hands-off so the table stopped building and let the push run cleanly. I kept the mood light and the table focused through the last two minutes.", "my_share_percent": 40}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table delivered a large, clear fish outline, with a rounded body, a swooshy tail and a nose, and nearly every standing domino was connected to the start for the push. I contributed to that by finding and fixing the break just before the nose, which had left the nose stretch disconnected from the start. I also closed a stray domino in the belly seam later on.

Execution: I spent my time on careful inspection of the run, checking it repeatedly from the start through the top line, nose, belly and tail to see what would actually fall. I restacked the three dominoes that needed standing back up, each at a spot where the fall had stalled. I also flagged an overlap at the belly ends so the bottom line would leave from a true end.

Collaboration: I kept hands off areas where teammates were working so we avoided bumping each other, and I told people before I touched a spot. I suggested splitting the long bottom line so Priya could carry the tail end back toward the belly while Maya worked on from the nose. That kept the work moving in the last five minutes. I also confirmed to the table when the nose was fixed so Tom could carry on.

Leadership: I helped set the sequence for the second half of the build: who carries which stretch, where they meet, and when everyone steps back. I called for hands off before the push so nothing got knocked at the last moment. I backed Priya's fish concept at the outset and kept the group focused on getting one connected run.

Overall, I think my inspection and the fixes at the nose and belly were central to getting the whole run to fall as one piece, though the fish itself was a team effort.", "my_share_percent": 30}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I carried the top line of the fish from the middle of the back round the curve to the nose, so the bottom line could start. Later I laid the tail from the peak of the bump down to the tip. Those two stretches make up the nose and the swooshy tail, which are the features that make the outline read as a fish. The start now reaches nearly all of the standing dominoes.

Execution: I worked in short batches and inspected the line often. I stood back up the dominoes that had fallen along my stretches and nudged a tight domino at the tail. I also closed a stray domino in the belly. In the last minutes I checked the tail tip so the fall would run through to the end. When time was close I stepped back and left the run alone.

Collaboration: I agreed early to the fish idea and kept clear of Maya's bottom line so we didn't bump each other. I took over Priya's top line when she asked, and I told the table when the line reached the nose so Maya could start. I also told the table when I took the tail so Priya and Leo knew where my hands were. I kept the updates short and clear.

Leadership: I took the top line and the tail without being assigned them, and I announced where I was working. This freed Priya and Maya to focus on the belly and the bottom line. I also called the hands-off moment before the push so nobody disturbed the run.", "my_share_percent": 27}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the bottom line of the fish, stroke 2. It forms the belly and the underside of the body, so it is a large part of what makes the outline read as a fish. I traced it from the nose and laid about 25 dominoes across several batches, then stood back up the few that were knocked over. The finished run falls from the start through nearly all of the standing dominoes.

Execution: I picked up the bottom line as soon as the top line reached the nose and worked on it steadily. After I laid the first stretch, I inspected the belly several times to find where the chain was weak. I stood dominoes back up where needed, so the belly stayed connected through to the push. When the time got tight, I handed the tail end to a teammate so the line could be finished from both directions. I stayed clear of the others' hands at the end so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I told the table early that I had the bottom line and kept them updated on where my line stopped. I agreed the handoff point for the tail end, so we avoided working within a few units of each other. I stepped back once the tail was being built, and I kept the table informed through to the final hands-off call.

Leadership: I took a defined piece of work, committed to it out loud, and delivered it. I made the handoff decision on the bottom line myself and then moved to checking joins. That kept the table's critical path moving and helped us finish with time to spare.", "my_share_percent": 28}
